content:
A new open-source tool has been circulating online recently, claiming to help users who have no interest in Apple Intelligence reclaim 12GB or more of storage on their Mac. Here are the details.

"Turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove downloaded models"

As with many companies adding various AI tools and models to their platforms, Apple has faced criticism because some features—deemed superfluous by certain users—are taking up storage space.

On macOS 26, Apple Intelligence takes up to 7GB of storage; however, with macOS 27, that figure has increased dramatically. Apple says its latest models can occupy up to 14GB of space on newer Macs.

In response to this issue, independent developer Om Lahore published a project called RemoveMacAI on GitHub at the end of last week, claiming it can "turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove downloaded models".

Lahore explained that his tool applies a configuration profile that uses Apple's own restriction keys to disable Apple Intelligence, while also using the company's asset service to remove downloaded models and prevent macOS from downloading them again.

He also detailed in full what the tool removes, which features it disables, and what users can expect after running it:

Features disabled: Siri (including "Hey Siri" and the menu bar icon), Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, ChatGPT extensions, summarisation features in Mail, Messages, Safari, Notes, and notifications, smart replies in Mail, inline text prediction, Spatial Photos, the Clean Up feature in Photos, and predictive code completion in Xcode. Models removed: The Apple Intelligence foundation model, as well as models used for image generation and Genmoji, Spatial Photos, the Clean Up feature in Photos, and code completion in Xcode.

And

Lahore noted that the Dictation function will still work after running RemoveMacAI, because "Dictation is a separate setting, and its language model is not removed".

Finally, he added that the entire process is reversible, with full details and instructions available here.

9to5Mac's take

Although some of the discontent with Apple Intelligence taking up storage on Mac seems to be the same instinctive backlash to anything AI-related, the argument does hold water for users with limited built-in storage—especially those with a 256GB Mac—where reclaiming 12GB or more makes a tangible difference.

A more fundamental issue is the basic control users have over their own operating system: users who have no interest in Apple Intelligence should have a straightforward way to turn it off completely and reclaim the storage its models occupy, just as they can with other apps and optional components in the system.

However, it remains unknown whether Apple will try to take the project down from GitHub, or change the underlying mechanisms in macOS to make it harder to remove the Apple Intelligence models.

Similarly, there is no way to know what impact disabling or removing these components will have on future versions of macOS itself, or potentially on third-party apps that increasingly rely on Apple models to provide basic functionality.

Although RemoveMacAI is open-source and does not require disabling System Integrity Protection (SIP), it still relies on configuration profiles, restriction keys, and system services—all of which Apple can change at any time.

Top comment posted by Piersandro

I don't use anything related to Apple AI on my own device.

I will definitely use this tool.

That means future macOS updates could break parts of the tool, and users might run into unexpected situations until the project is updated.

At this stage, anyone considering using RemoveMacAI should understand that it is an unofficial third-party tool that makes changes at the system level, and users should be fully aware of how it works.

Ultimately, RemoveMacAI appears to be a well-intentioned open-source project aimed at giving Mac users more autonomy and control over what runs on their computer and how their storage is used. Whether Apple will see it the same way remains to be seen.
